I am 73 this year, and I have worked my 3 mu in Quzhou County for 55 years. I only finished primary school, but the land taught me the rest. My wife and I do all the labor ourselves. We have a well for irrigation, but pumping costs diesel, so I count every drop.

I start from what I did last year. Last year my wheat gave me about 950 jin per mu, and my maize gave about 1,100 jin per mu. This year I will do almost the same, because change is risky and I know this works.

For wheat: I sow in mid-October, right after the summer maize comes off. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town, about 25 jin per mu — 75 jin total for my 3 mu. Before sowing, I spread base fertilizer: 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. I buy three 50 kg bags. That is about 450 yuan, but I do not dare skip it. At green-up time around March, I topdress with urea, about 50 jin per mu. I buy two 40 kg bags and spread them across the 3 mu. Irrigating three times: once in winter if it is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide right after sowing, and one spray in spring for aphids or rust if I see them. I expect about 950 jin per mu again.

For maize: In early June, as soon as the wheat is cut, I rotary-till and sow the same day. I buy hybrid corn seed every year, about 6 jin per mu, 18 jin total. At sowing I put down 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. Then when the corn reaches big trumpet stage, I chase it with urea, about 60 jin per mu. Corn needs food at that stage or the ears will be small. My neighbor Lao Wang cut his urea last year and regretted it. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come — once at jointing, once at filling. Two sprays: herbicide after emergence, and one for corn borer. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu.

Money is tight on 3 mu. The fertilizer alone costs me over 800 yuan for both crops. But a bad harvest is a disaster. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than sleep hungry next winter. I watch what my neighbors do, and around here we all plant and fertilize about the same. If Lao Zhang and Old Liu are putting down 100 jin of compound on their wheat, so do I.
